issue.title: Decide: element↔review-object sync model
issue.body:
## Question

Essence B means canonical review state stays in Rennet while board cards present/reference it. How do cards reference review objects, how is staleness handled when the underlying object changes, and what does the import layer own?

Blocked by #455

comments.body:
**Resolved (2026-08-23).** The "sync model" the ticket was named for dissolves: there is no sync, because the board is the store.

## Model

- **Two stores.** Board event logs = canonical review content (Rennet persists them). The immutable patchset / git = the code. Code-blocks bridge the two by citing into the patchset; no shadow review store sits behind the boards.
- **Element = block.** Atomic content unit like a React component or a headless-CMS / Notion block. `kind` = block type (heading, paragraph, code, callout, badge, lens-container, …); element-typed attributes give the block tree (nesting + order). A lens report is a block document of many elements. A single finding is a small cluster of blocks (heading + prose + code-block + badge), not one element.
- **Only Lens outputs become blocks.** Delta (the context maps) and Shadow stay context the drafting agent reads — never projected onto a board.
- **Topology A.** Each lens is its own board, drafted by a review agent on a fixed prompt (L2). The orchestrator **authors** a separate composition Board (L3) *from* the frozen lens drafts — composition is authoring, not cross-board reference. Every board is self-contained; drafts sit behind the composition as drill-down provenance. No partitions, no access rules (the partition-canvas rot stays dead).
- **Code citation.** A code-block's data carries `(patchset ref, path, span)` into the immutable patchset; the renderer pretty-prints the real lines. Code is never copied into the block.
- **Data direction.** Review-derived blocks flow Rennet→board. Board-native data (human curation: marks, groupings, arrangement, notes) is authored on the board and is **live input the orchestrator gathers to compose the review** — it never mutates draft/lens content.
- **Change handling: append-then-freeze.** Within one patchset's review, boards stay live append-only logs — re-running a lens appends, and curation on surviving block ids persists. When the code moves (successor patchset), the generation **freezes** immutable and a new generation is minted; the **successor account** (renamed from delta re-review) compares generation N vs N+1. Reversible lifecycle policy, not a protocol change.

## Vocabulary locked

- **"card" is dead** — a presentation word; how an element is drawn is the renderer's choice, not a model concept.
- **element = block**; **lens = a drafted board/report**; **generation = the boards for one review of one patchset**; **board-native data = human curation the orchestrator composes from**.
- The re-review "delta" is renamed **successor account**, ending the collision with pipeline **Delta** (the change-vs-baseline context maps). `packages/core/src/delta-account.ts` and the delta-re-review docs get the rename when touched.

## Handed off / graduated

- "What does the import layer own" (partition-canvas replacement) → #459, not this ticket.
- The Rennet board **host schema** (the block kinds) is now specifiable → #462.

issue.title: Decide: Rennet import plan — replacing the partition canvas
issue.body:
## Question

The shipped canvas model (types/src/index.ts:1051-1069, core/src/canvas.ts) is rot: actor partition made structural. Decide what replaces it when whiteboard lands: type migration, what of the projector/app-ui survives, how CanvasAngle/lenses re-anchor onto the Board, deletion inventory.

Carried in from #457 (element↔review-object sync model): the re-review "delta" is renamed **successor account** to end the collision with pipeline **Delta**. This inventory owns the rename — `packages/core/src/delta-account.ts` and the delta-re-review docs — as part of the migration.

Blocked by #455, #457

comments.body:
**Resolved (2026-08-23).** Clean cutover to the Board model — the partition canvas is deleted wholesale, no dual-model coexistence. This ticket produces the plan + deletion inventory; execution is downstream.

## Decisions

- **Scope**: plan-only. Output = this decision + deletion inventory + OpenSpec-ready migration spec. Execution is a downstream build.
- **Shape**: clean cutover. Delete the partition-canvas model wholesale; no strangler / flagged coexistence period.
- **Sequencing**: planning proceeds now, unblocked. Execution consumes the *published* `@whiteboard/core` per #456 (+ `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`); no local-link shortcut.
- **successor-account rename folded in**: `packages/core/src/delta-account.ts` + `docs/developing/concepts/delta-rereview-and-lineage.md` renamed as part of this migration, not deferred to "when touched" (#457).
- **Disposition dissolves**: delete the `Disposition` type, `DispositionLayer`, and `canvas.disposition`. A human verdict becomes **board-native data** the orchestrator composes from — no sovereign L2 gate (Rule Zero: NO GATES).
- **`CanvasAngle` → `LensKind`**: keep the five-value union (`spec|sequence|decisions|noise|flagged`) as lens identity; delete `DOC_TYPE_ANGLE` and the whole `buildCanvas` projector. Deterministic doc→angle placement dies with the canvas.
- **Scope line vs drafting**: #459 covers type/surface migration + re-anchorability *only*. Content derivations survive as surface-agnostic element producers. The L2/L3 lens-board drafting-agent architecture is a **new ticket, blocked by #460** (the cheap→expensive swarm layer sits below where whiteboard is relevant).
- **All six `canvas.*` protocol commands die**: board-native writes route through #455's whiteboard authoring tools. `pinAnnotation` → annotation element; `select` / `setCohortExpansion` → UI-only read-state (#462); `adjudicateProposal` + the `Proposal*` family → gone (orchestrator authors the composition Board directly); `disposition` → gone. No parallel Rennet canvas-command surface.

## Deletion inventory (adopted from the code census)

**[DELETE]**
- `packages/types/src/index.ts:1050-2118` — `Canvas` root (:1982), the 4 layer types (Substrate/Analysis/Disposition/Annotation), `CanvasAngle`/`CANVAS_ANGLES`, `AnalysisElement`/`AnalysisCohort`, `Proposal*`, `BlastRadiusPaint`, `CanvasChangeNotification`
- `packages/core/src/canvas.ts` — the whole projector (`buildCanvas`, `DOC_TYPE_ANGLE`, `projectAnalysis`, fold + dispatch ops)
- `packages/core/src/canvas-ops.ts`, `packages/core/src/canvas-change-feed.ts`
- `packages/adapters/src/canvas-ops-*.ts` (+ the index re-export)
- `packages/protocol/src/index.ts:317-438` — canvas schema, `review.canvases`, the six `canvas.*` commands
- `packages/app-ui/src/canvas/*`, `components/workspace.tsx`, `lens.tsx`, `flat.tsx`, the per-angle renderers + related index exports
- `apps/mobile/.../review/[reviewId]/canvas.tsx` + `apps/mobile/src/lib/canvas-rows.ts`
- docs `docs/developing/concepts/canvas-model.md`, `review-lenses.md` (rewrite via downstream docs-refresh)

**[REWORK — keep the logic, re-anchor off canvas onto Board/Lens]**
- `CanvasAngle` → `LensKind` (rename, keep 5 values)
- content derivations `app-ui/src/canvas/{flagged,noise,collation,counterpart,openspec}.ts` → emit elements, not canvas placements
- `pipeline.ts` terminal placement step (drop the `buildCanvas` call)
- `server/create-server.ts` `buildCanvases*` entrypoints + `dispatch.ts` wiring
- narration keyed on cohortKey/rollup → re-anchor
- `delta-account.ts` → **successor-account** rename (file + docs)

**[KEEP untouched]**
- findings / decisions (+evidence/why) / noise verdicts / requirements / `ElementDiff` — review content, surface-agnostic
- `server/projection.ts` — unrelated path-privacy projector
- blast-radius signal taxonomy (drop only the "paint as overlay" framing)

## Graduated / handed off
- New ticket: **Decide: lens-board drafting-agent architecture (L2 draft boards + L3 composition)** — blocked by #460.
- Docs rewrites (`canvas-model.md`, `review-lenses.md`) + the delta-doc rename → downstream docs-refresh, not a wayfinder decision.
Resolved — see resolution comment. Clean cutover to Board; deletion inventory adopted; drafting-agent architecture graduated to a new ticket blocked by #460.

issue.title: Decide: context-map swarm architecture
issue.body:
## Question

Replace the single flat knowledge pass (DEFAULT_KNOWLEDGE_MAX_FILES=400, knowledge-generation.ts:49) with the intended design: swarm of cheap models doing partitioned local passes feeding a medium/large connect-the-dots model. Total coverage by partitioning, not sampling. Decide the fan-out shape, model tiers, cost envelope, and how output feeds L0 Shadow / L1 Delta.

comments.body:
Resolved 2026-08-24 (grill with Rai + prior-art sweep). The architecture:

**1. Partition = the scope graph, and it is invisible plumbing.** One worker per scope from the structural map; oversized scopes subtree-split under a per-worker file cap (~120 files); plain directory split as the fallback when scope detection finds nothing. Coverage is total by construction — every file in exactly one slice. No partition-shaped artifact survives the run: the map's output stays scopes + statements (nothing like the killed partition canvas).

**2. Workers emit full statements at the edge.** Light-tier workers read their slice and emit the existing statement schema (subject / aspect / claim / confidence / evidence anchors), with the shipped honesty contract at mint time (anchors resolved to blobOids, anchor-or-drop, hypothesis label). Plus one optional `hint` field — a free-text nudge for the synthesizer, discardable, never stored.

**3. Medium model verifies and connects — hypotheses are NOT gated on human intervention (Rai's ruling).** The verify/synthesis seat (a) re-reads each hypothesis's cited evidence spans and flips it to confirmed or rejected itself — bounded by anchors, not a repo re-read; (b) mints the cross-cutting statements no single worker could see; (c) dedups. The map surface's confirm/reject stays as an optional human override on top of model verdicts — never a gate; the map is fully useful the moment the run finishes.

**4. Model tiers come from the Model Council — "we already have a map for this" (Rai).** Knowledge work stops bypassing the council (today `enrichKnowledgeForRepo` runs on the bare Claude harness default with no job id — the one off-council asymmetry). New job ids enter the three versioned tables in `packages/core/src/model-council.ts`: a light-tier partition-worker job (both-scenario: cheap Codex, `gpt-5.6-luna`/`terra`) and a heavy verify/synthesis job (both-scenario: Claude `sonnet-5`). claude-only / codex-only tables cover single-harness installs; the degraded default applies when neither; `routing.task.<jobId>` overrides exist by construction. No new settings surface. Prior art: `docs/developing/concepts/model-council.md`, `openspec/specs/model-council{,-live}/spec.md`, `packages/core/src/{model-council,dual-seat,codex-utility-port}.ts`.

**5. No cost cap.** First map generation is allowed to be expensive; enrichment never degrades by sampling or partition omission (the 400-file git-order cap and its silent ~10% coverage are the bug this kills). R10 budget refusal does not gate this path — consistent with the shipped spec's "uncapped, off the critical path".

**6. Incremental thereafter (the delta is partition-routed).** On baseline advance: only workers whose slice contains changed paths re-run; the verify seat re-adjudicates only statements whose cited evidence changed; everything else carries verbatim (shipped carry semantics, localized). Cross-cutting statements re-verify when any cited path changed.

**7. Knowledge reaches the review agents.** L0 Shadow = structural map + this knowledge set, standing per project. L2 lens agents receive the resolved statements for the scopes the diff touches plus the cross-cutting set — bounded payload, fixes the second half of the original bug (agents got a static summary only).

**8. Run surface.** Progress shows per-partition workers (queued / running / statement counts) and the verify/synthesis stage as its own lines — prototyped on #458.

Unblocks #464 (lens drafting-agent architecture).

issue.title: Decide: lens-board drafting-agent architecture (L2 draft boards + L3 composition)
issue.body:
## Question

Design the L2/L3 lens-board drafting-agent architecture. From #457: each lens is its own **draft board (L2)** drafted by a review agent on a fixed prompt, and the orchestrator **authors** the **composition Board (L3)** from the frozen drafts (compose-by-authoring, no cross-board refs).

Decide: what each drafting agent receives; how the surface-agnostic content derivations kept by #459 (`flagged`/`noise`/`collation`/`counterpart`/`openspec`) feed the drafting agents vs. are replaced by agent authoring; the draft → freeze → compose flow and where board-native human curation enters the composition; and how this consumes the swarm output from #460 (cheap-model partitioned passes → medium/large connect-the-dots).

Blocked by #460 (the cheap→expensive context-map swarm sits a layer below and defines what feeds drafting).

comments.body:
## Implementation dossier (2026-08-24 session) — everything the drafting architecture must honor

Decided and dogfooded this session. Full ruling log lives on the canonical #458 comment (R17–R22 + trial reports); this is the implementer-facing digest. Planned-behavior docs: `docs/developing/concepts/lens-pipeline.md`.

### Fixed inputs to this design

- **Lens set + order**: Design, Sequence, Decisions, Flagged, Noise (Design first; renamed from spec / reading-order).
- **Prompts are product content**: `packages/lens-instructions` — one markdown prompt per lens + `unslop-pass.md` (the unslop skill verbatim). Typed manifest in `src/index.ts`. The board schema travels separately from the instruction bytes (same anti-drift rule as the old RSP contract).
- **Pipeline per generation**: draft (1 agent per lens; Flagged = two independent seats, Claude + Codex) → reconcile Flagged (merge shared root causes, record per-finding concurrence, rejected candidates go to a cleared-concerns block with reasoning) → unslop editor pass over every draft (prose fields only; typed data byte-untouched) → orchestrator composes the Board from frozen drafts (#457).
- **Dogfood evidence**: two full runs against real merged PR #438 produced honest boards, converged dual seats, and one real bug (#478). The prompts work; keep their text under version control and treat edits as product changes.

### Rules the runtime must enforce (not just prompt-request)

- **R17 no authored conversations**: drafting agents can never emit thread/message elements — reject at validation, not just instruction.
- **R18 lanes**: out-of-lane material is omitted, never narrated. No remainder prose.
- **R19 coverage as data**: every draft board carries `skippedHunks` ({path, reason}); composition asserts every patchset hunk ∈ some lens's taught-or-skipped set. R22: generated scaffold stamps (`.openspec.yaml` etc.) are Noise's lane.
- **R20 voice**: third person about the change; board prose never names lenses/boards/agents/process.
- **R21 projection**: spec-stated decisions render on Design (artifact content) AND Decisions (the call, citing the artifact); both boards self-contained.
- **Citations**: prose citations are full repo-relative `path:line` so the UI can resolve them (click-to-reveal reads the real file).

### Block anatomy decisions (feed #462's host schema when it gets revisited)

- **finding**: short claim body + `details` (one subheaded part per failure member) + `fix` (own field, rendered as an actionable callout) + anchor + per-seat concurrence. Not a boxed card in the UI — document flow.
- **decision**: statement / why / inferred flag / alternatives / evidence anchors + `excerpts` (one code slice per evidence site → tabbed viewer).
- **requirement**: name + delta (added/modified/removed) + verbatim normative text + scenarios + coverage {hunks, tests} + refs.
- **Design lens spec-header**: change name, capability counts, task rollup, distilled why, format + source chip, artifact-set jump chips (proposal/design/specs/tasks; absent artifact = no chip).
- Open question (flagged earlier on #458): do spec-header / what-changes / capability-grid / task-progress become host-schema kinds or orchestrator-authored compositions?

### UI affordances the boards assume (prototyped in spikes/board-prototype)

- Rich prose: backticks → monospace; `path:line` → click-to-reveal inline code (spike: `components/rich-text.tsx` + `/api/source`; real app resolves through the patchset/code-ref layer instead).
- Tabbed code viewer for multi-site evidence (`components/code-tabs.tsx`, quiet pill tabs, sans labels).
- Fold gist + counts per section; provenance chips (`source`) on artifact-backed sections; add-green delta edges.

### Known boundary cases for this design to settle

- Shared-hunk lane arbitration beyond R22 (the `.openspec.yaml` collision pattern).
- What each drafting agent receives (blocked by #460) and how the surviving core derivations (finding/decision/noise/decomposition/blast-radius) feed or get replaced.

## Addendum (Rai, 2026-08-24): enforcement layers — prompt rules become guarantees

Rai's requirement: the presentation/voice rules must hold at implementation time, not by fixture surgery. Three layers, all required:

1. **Schema** — good structure is the only expressible structure. `code-ref` (path + span + highlights, surface-hydrated) replaces agent-typed code bytes everywhere; finding has `fix` and `details` as fields; `skippedHunks` is a field. Illegal states unrepresentable (feeds #462).
2. **Board lint** — a deterministic validation stage between draft and unslop, rejecting: thread/message kinds from drafting agents (R17), code bytes instead of code refs (R25/R26), unresolvable citations, missing/incomplete `skippedHunks` (R19, with the cross-lens every-hunk check at composition), prose-wall findings (fix or scenario members buried in body), and a process-vocabulary screen (lens/board/agent/seat/draft in prose, R20). Lint failure returns the draft to its agent with the violation named — a retry loop, not a silent patch.
3. **Editorial** — the unslop pass now carries an explicit de-meta instruction (delete surviving machinery-narration sentences; third person only), so judgment-only rules have an owner too.

Rule of thumb recorded in docs (`lens-pipeline.md`, updated): **a rule that lives in a prompt alone is a wish.**

Also corrected from earlier today: code is NOT on-demand-only. Code stays woven in the reading flow (law 5) as hydrated code refs — the earlier "cite and click to reveal" over-correction is withdrawn; the withdrawn part is inline *bytes*, not inline *code*.

Unblocked: [the context-map swarm decision](https://github.com/rbutera/rennet/issues/460#issuecomment-5409482209) is resolved. Load-bearing context for this ticket that the issue tracker didn't previously carry:

- **Model selection is the Model Council's job** — `docs/developing/concepts/model-council.md`, normative specs `openspec/specs/model-council{,-live}/spec.md`, versioned tables in `packages/core/src/model-council.ts`. Lens drafting agents should resolve seats through council job ids (as Flagged's dual seats already do via `resolveDualSeat`), not name models. Three scenarios (both / claude-only / codex-only) come free.
- **Knowledge now reaches the lens agents**: per the #460 resolution, L2 drafting agents receive the resolved knowledge statements for the scopes the diff touches plus the cross-cutting set — design the drafting-agent inputs against that, not the old static summary.
- Lens prompts + unslop pass live in `packages/lens-instructions` (2026-08-24 session, rulings R17–R22 on #458).

Hand-off design (R29–R34, 2026-08-25) touches this architecture in two places: (1) a versioned **orchestrator prompt** joins packages/lens-instructions — staging judgment (stage on stated conclusions/shortcuts, offer on inference) and living-draft authorship rules live there, versioned like the lens prompts; (2) **delta-aware generation drafting** is now load-bearing: each work-order round mints a new board generation and drafters receive the successor account, carrying unchanged sections forward verbatim — the drafting architecture must support scoped redrafting, not just full regeneration. Full design: docs/developing/concepts/handoff-and-exits.md.

Pipeline amendment for the implementer dossier: the unslop stage is now the **post-process pass** (R39 on the #458 ruling log). `packages/lens-instructions` — `prompts/post-process.md` (break-it-down + unslop verbatim + humanizer additions), `prompts/review-draft-voice.md` (orchestrator write-through rules for the living review draft), manifest exports `POST_PROCESS_FILE` + `REVIEW_DRAFT_VOICE_FILE` (`UNSLOP_PASS_FILE` is gone). Docs: `docs/developing/concepts/lens-pipeline.md` step 4 rewritten.

Seat note from R57 on #458 ([#486](https://github.com/rbutera/rennet/issues/486)): the **round-report drafter** is a per-round seat beside the five lens drafters — prompt `ROUND_REPORT_FILE` (`prompts/report.md`) in `rennet-lens-instructions`, post-process pass applies. Hard ordering for this architecture: when a round returns, the report drafts FIRST (it verifies each ask against the round's diff — never the worker's word — and its frozen output IS the successor account R34 says the lens drafters receive). So the drafting flow is: report → parallel lens drafters (carried lenses carry forward, touched lenses re-draft) → post-process → composition; and the composition step stamps section `delta: "new" | "reworked"` (R58) as a side effect of its carry-vs-redraft decision — it knows this for free, no extra analysis.

## Resolution (2026-08-26, grilled with Rai)

Pipeline order and enforcement layers stand as previously fixed (report-first on rounds per R57; schema / board-lint / editorial per the enforcement addendum). The nine decisions:

1. **Drafter runtime.** Each lens drafter is a real harness session in the PR worktree — it needs file reads to mint resolvable `path:line` citations — seeded warm with an inlined **Delta packet**: the patchset, touched-scope + cross-cutting knowledge statements (#460 §7), the related-context dossier (#461), the successor account on rounds (the round report, R57), and its lens prompt + host schema.

2. **Deterministic derivations feed, agents author.** The #459 survivors run as producers whose typed facts enter the drafter packet as candidate data — never hand-retyped, and doubling as validation inputs. `openspec` parse → Design drafter (artifact set, requirement deltas); noise rules pre-classify (lockfiles, R22 stamps), the agent judges the remainder, the verdict records which judged; `collation`/`counterpart` → Sequence hints, with collation also powering the composition-side every-hunk check; `flagged` shrinks to the severity projection of findings (#462) — the lens itself is pure dual-seat authoring.

3. **Structured return, not tool-authoring (Rai ruling).** Drafters return schema-validated structured output (Zod/Pydantic); the host writes it to the draft board as ops on their behalf. The whiteboard authoring tools exist for the orchestrator and the human — agentic tool-calling per element is inefficient and expensive. R58 progressive reveal becomes per-board/per-section arrival as the host applies each draft.

4. **Composition splits mechanical vs authored.** Code does the bookkeeping: every-hunk coverage assertion, verbatim section carry on stable ids, `delta: new|reworked` stamps. The orchestrator authors only the rest — new/reworked content, ordering, rollups — on a versioned `composition` prompt joining `lens-instructions`. Human curation (board-native data, #457) enters the next generation's composition packet as structured input. Never pay a model to copy text it must not change.

5. **Model Council job ids.** `lens-draft` (Design/Sequence/Decisions), `lens-draft-flagged` (existing dual-seat path), `lens-draft-noise` (light), `board-post-process`, `round-report`. Composition rides the orchestrator's own session — no new id.

6. **Lane arbitration.** Overlap is legal — one hunk taught from two angles is product. Only **gaps** violate: the every-hunk check finds a hunk skipped by all lenses → it returns to the lens the skip reasons name (Sequence as default owner) for a scoped redraft. Recurring collisions graduate into standing lane rules in the prompts, as R22 did.

7. **Spec top-matter = compositions, palette stays closed.** Spec-header / what-changes / capability-grid / task-progress are assembled from the existing #462 kinds (`section`/`prose`/`callout` + typed attrs). Criterion (Rai): consistency and portability across spec libraries (openspec, superpowers, amazon kiro, grill-with-docs, and whatever joins) — typed kinds stay format-agnostic; the Design prompt + spec-format survey absorb per-format differences.

8. **Retry loop: cap 10, escape hatch not gate.** Lint returns only the violating elements with the exact rule named. On exhaustion the draft freezes as-is and violations ride into the board as visible defect data — the review proceeds, never blocks. Deep design (cheap retries, hard to fail, slop-tight, telemetry to tune the cap) → #493.

9. **Topology A amended: there is no sixth board.** The five lens boards are the reading surface; four scenarios of dogfood never missed a composed surface. "Composition" names the orchestrator's connective authoring across them — the coverage assertion, carry + delta stamps, rollups, the sequence spine — plus the hand-off drafts it authors (living drafts, asks). #457's composition-Board-as-surface language is superseded; CONTEXT.md glossary update follows in-repo.

Ripples: #493 unblocks (dispatching). #462 untouched (palette closed confirmed). #489 consumes all of this as the drafting-architecture input.
